correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge3\) and \(g>0\), the Fourier decomposition gives \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) distinct nonuniform rim eigenvalues and the two hybrid levels. Only one lower-hybrid collision is possible and its coupling is explicit. Absorber-evaluation ranks on the collided eigenspace give exactly a one-dimensional single-rim deficit and no deficit for rim+hub. The explicit hub projection in a two-coordinate collision plane gives the survival fraction; a sine bound gives the high-protection sequence. Dissipativity proves that the spectral dark projector equals infinite-time survival. Original package verify.py numerically compares complete Hamiltonian eigenprojectors for \(3\le n\le30\) (84 generic, 119 resonance, 203 double-sink checks). This is corroboration, not an infinite certificate.

value.rationale: The exact natural invariant (infinite-time absorption of a wheel quantum excitation) has sharp parameter-dependent discontinuities and state-specific consequences: at finite isolated spoke strengths the hub can evade a directly adjacent rim sink, with survival approaching unity as wheel size increases, whereas all nearby positive couplings give complete eventual capture. An added hub sink restores exactly one lost capture dimension. This quantitative network-control boundary is more informative than a routine numerical spectral listing, although it is idealized and finite-time robustness is not claimed.
